title: Orion Health - Incident postmortem follow-up
summary: Follow-up on the 2027-10-03 production incident affecting inference latency and tail error rates. Reviewed root cause (autoscaler bug + cache eviction), mitigations already applied, next steps for reliability improvements, SLAs / credits discussion, and scheduling for joint runbook and load tests.
topics: Root cause: autoscaler config + KV cache eviction bug
Mitigations applied: hotfix, scaling policy adjustment, backbone alerting
Reliability improvements: runbooks, synthetic tests, blue/green failover
Security and compliance: audit logs, KMS verification
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-10-10
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Orion Head of Platform), Marcus Lee (Orion SRE), Elena Ruiz (Orion Security)
Links shared: postmortem doc: https://redwood.ai/postmortems/orion-2027-10-03, s3 logs link: (redacted), runbook draft: https://redwood.ai/runbooks/orion-runbook-draft

00:00 Alex: ok hey everyone thanks for jumping on, this is Alex from Redwood, i think we scheduled 55 minutes to go through the followup on the outage from last week and make sure any remaining action items are clear
00:12 Priya: thanks Alex, appreciate it. we already got the initial postmortem but wanted to run through the RCA w/ the SEs and make sure the fixes are durable and that we have a plan for future prevention
00:25 Samir: yeah hi team, Samir here, i'll start with a quick recap of what we found and then we can go into mitigations and next steps
00:38 Samir: so root cause — there were two compounding issues: one, an autoscaler threshold misconfiguration on the dedicated pool in us-west-2 that caused slower scale-up under a spike; two, a KV cache eviction bug in our inference runtime that led to higher cold-start work for some session types, so the observed tail latency spiked and some requests timed out
01:12 Marcus: can i interrupt — when you say misconfiguration, was that human error or a deploy that changed defaults?
01:20 Samir: good q, it was a deploy that inadvertently changed the scaleUp cool-down parameters; it was pushed as part of a separate optimization change. config drift + insufficient canary rules. so primarily process + a bad default that slipped through code review
01:36 Elena: From security perspective we were also worried about audit trail — do we have immutable logs for the autoscaler change?
01:44 Alex: yes we do, we pulled the infra audit logs; they'll be in the postmortem appendix. there was a note about the change id and user. we'll share the exact log links after the call
01:55 Priya: and the KV cache eviction — what's that? Marcus: can you elaborate Samir?
02:03 Samir: so the cache eviction was triggered by a race where session tokens were marked stale prematurely, in some cases the KV cache cleanup job ran while the session had a pending async request; that forced the runtime to recompute context and rehydrate weights which is expensive. some of the naming in the logs is messy — KV cash in a few entries — so the transcriber might say cash, haha
02:30 Marcus: okay that explains the repeated model loads we saw. did that hit specific models or all of them?
02:37 Samir: mostly the long-context conversation models — ones with large KV footprints. we saw it on model rdx-3b and rdx-10b variants running quantized paths. smaller models less affected
02:48 Priya: what mitigations have you applied so far?
02:52 Samir: immediate hotfix: reverted the autoscaler deploy to previous cooldown, patched the cache cleanup job to add a distributed lock so it won't run if there's an in-progress session, and we rolled a runtime patch to make the cache refcounting more conservative. deployed to dedicated pool and verified in staging then prod canary
03:18 Alex: we also temporarily increased headroom for the dedicated pool to give extra capacity during the transit period — that cost spike is on us, we'll reconcile that in the billing discussion
03:30 Priya: appreciate that. our only concern is recurrence during business hours; last outage hit our live clinic workflows which is high impact
03:38 Samir: agreed, which is why we have follow-up items: synthetic traffic tests for the long-context paths, better canarying for infra changes that touch scaling defaults, and an automated guard that will revert scaling parameter changes if a latency SLO breach is detected in the canary window
03:59 Marcus: can you give timelines for those? we need to schedule acceptance tests from our side
04:05 Alex: sure, Samir — do you want to take the rough timeboxes?
04:10 Samir: runbook update and draft for synthetic tests — 1 week; automated guard prototype — 2 weeks; full CI canary gating policy — ~3 weeks. we can frontload the runbook and synthetic tests so Orion can run acceptance earlier
04:28 Priya: that works, we can allocate Marcus and one dev to help with the acceptance tests next Tuesday if you can share the test harness
04:36 Alex: noted. we'll share the harness link and a how-to doc.
04:40 Elena: security followups — Elena here — we need confirmation that no PII was written to any third-party logs during the incident and also we want the KMS key rotation audit that was mentioned in the postmortem
04:52 Alex: good call. Samir, can you confirm the logs and KMS note?
04:57 Samir: yes — we audited application logs and confirmed no PII was emitted; the external logs were our infra level aggregated metrics; detailed request bodies are not in those logs. KMS rotation: we have short-term scheduled rotation but not an immediate rotate; i can push a rotation plan and timeline and provide the audit entries.
05:16 Elena: we'll need those entries for our compliance team; can you add them to the security appendix?
05:20 Alex: yes we will add to the appendix and share the link.
05:25 Priya: about SLA credits — do we have a process for that? last postmortem mentioned credits being evaluated
05:30 Alex: yep — for Dedicated customers we evaluate incident severity and downtime impact; we will calculate credit for the window where latency exceeded SLOs. i'll follow up with a formal calculation, but the draft will be shared by 2027-10-12
05:44 Priya: thank you. also on runbook, we'd like explicit steps for failover to a different region and how Redwood handles KV cache warmup — that was a pain point
05:54 Samir: good point — we're adding region failover steps and pre-warm hooks so when a failover occurs the system will prefetch hot keys. that pre-warm will be part of the runbook and the synthetic tests will validate it
06:10 Marcus: one more question on metrics — can we get a token-level breakdown? our engineers wanted the per-token latency histogram not just p95/p99
06:18 Alex: we can share more granular traces and histograms. some are in the postmortem but we'll pull the raw dashboards for you (redacted link)
06:26 Priya: any blockers from Redwood side for the timelines you mentioned?
06:30 Samir: main blocker is engineering capacity for the guard and CI gating; we've prioritized it but if Orion can accept a staged rollout that reduces immediate pressure; we also want to coordinate test windows to avoid tripping your load
06:46 Priya: we can do staged acceptance. also request: please add our on-call SRE to the alerting distribution list for these infra alerts
06:55 Alex: we'll add Marcus and one more — who else?
06:58 Marcus: add Priya and Daniel Kim (I'll add him to the shared doc)
07:04 Alex: got it, we'll ensure alerting lists updated and share the updated alert policy doc
07:11 Elena: small nit — in the postmortem there are a couple of typos in variable names and one place it says KV "cash" which might freak out auditors, can you fix that?
07:20 Alex: yes we'll clean up the doc text and ensure consistent naming.
07:24 Priya: can we recap the concrete next steps and owners?
07:28 Alex: i'll read them out then Samir will add technical owners — next steps: 1) Send updated postmortem with security appendix and logs link. 2) Share synthetic test harness and runbook draft. 3) Prototype automated guard for scaler changes and timeline. 4) Provide SLA credit calculation. 5) Schedule joint runbook and load test acceptance.
07:52 Samir: tech owners: 1) Postmortem update — Alex (owner) + Samir (technical review) by 2027-10-12. 2) Synthetic harness & runbook draft — Samir (owner) with Orion input by 2027-10-17. 3) Guard prototype — Samir + infra team by 2027-10-24. 4) SLA calc — Alex by 2027-10-12. 5) Joint acceptance test — schedule for week of 2027-10-18, Marcus to confirm exact date.
08:20 Priya: ok thanks, that's clear. any other items?
08:24 Marcus: just a note — we want a monthly check-in for the next quarter to track these reliability improvements
08:30 Alex: happy to schedule a 30-minute monthly sync — i'll send recurring invites for Nov/Dec/Jan
08:38 Elena: one last ask — can Redwood share a short blameless summary slide for our execs?
08:44 Alex: yes we'll produce a 1-page blameless executive summary and include the timeline and mitigation actions
08:50 Priya: great, thanks everyone
08:53 Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and action items

Note: transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., KV cash/cash, misc punctuation).
